channel.title: Comments for page "Ambrose Three Portlands"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Ambrose Three Portlands"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm kinda, really torn on this: the writing is great and I dig what you've attempted to do here; but at the same time, I can't help but feel that this is like, the cliffs notes of the story over the actual story. All the like, actually interesting stuff which happens is elided in favour of summarising them in alternative sources and it leaves me wanting more from this.

Y'know, I started writing this comment as a firm novote but I think, on balance, it's going to be a -1 from me with a hope that you do more with this :(

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I wanted to explain my downvote because I was actually very torn on this article.

On the one hand I think the formatting is gorgeous. The Ambrose internal document looks great and the newspaper is such an excellent touch.

On the other hand, I just feel like this boils down to “this thing is gonna go wrong… look, it went wrong”

There lacks a narrative or characters for me to get attached to. If in between the Ambrose document and the newspaper clipping there was narrative explored concerning the experiences this product was producing (say in the form of yelp reviews?) this could be a really killer article.

But as it stands i felt this was a waste of a really good set up and excellent aesthetic.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: As a rewrite of what came before, it's definitely better. But judging it separately from that… it just doesn't really do much. I do like Ambrose docs, but this feels a little bit too one-note to make it.

item.content:encoded:
i like that it's not just a menu like the other Ambrose GoI formats - the main complaint i have with them is that they're so same-y, and this breaks the mold. IDK if there's any precedent but you could also probably tag this with "_deer-college", since it's both, even though it's mostly Ambrose.

One quibble though:

food trucks

No Cars In Three Ports (although "food carts" doesnt have the same sort of Portland resonance so maybe it's fine. they could be horse-drawn or pedal-powered or something.)
